open_points.subject: Import concurrency across owner sessions
open_points.text: “Uploads and import confirmations of all sessions take one lock of the instance” does not say how that lock composes with A13’s per-owner-session lock, while an accepted confirmation also “drops the uploaded file of every owner session.”
open_points.question: In what order are the instance lock and owner-session locks acquired, and must an accepted import lock every affected session before clearing its file?
options: Acquire the instance lock before any session lock and clear all files while holding it
Acquire the submitting session lock first, then the instance lock, and mutate other sessions without their locks
Acquire the instance lock and then every affected session lock in a declared order
open_points.default_guess: Acquire the instance lock first, then any required session locks in stable session-id order, and hold them through the all-session cleanup.

open_points.subject: Owner-only configuration
open_points.text: Rule 1 permits “for an owner-only start, none of the four” service tokens, but rule 2 requires “every item of rule 1 present” and rule 5 says “A missing ... item fails the start.”
open_points.question: Are all four service-token items explicitly exempt from the presence check when all four are absent, or must every configured start contain them?
options: Permit exactly two modes: all four tokens present or all four absent
Require all four tokens on every start
Permit any subset of tokens
open_points.default_guess: Permit exactly all four or none, rejecting partial sets.

open_points.subject: Configuration validation
open_points.text: Registry checks that “each [item is] well formed,” but no rule defines well formedness for the owner credential, service tokens, backup key, store location or backup location beyond the separate length and path checks.
open_points.question: What exact syntax, encoding and structural conditions make each configuration item well formed?
options: Only the checks explicitly stated elsewhere apply
Define additional per-item syntax and encoding rules
Treat every nonempty environment value as well formed before the later checks
open_points.default_guess: Use UTF-8 environment strings; require nonempty path values and apply no secret-format rule beyond byte length and distinctness.

open_points.subject: Secret length and equality
open_points.text: A secret is required to be “at least 32 bytes long,” although configuration values are environment-variable text and the text does not define their byte encoding or whether equality is measured before or after any decoding.
open_points.question: How are environment-variable secret values converted to bytes for the length, equality and constant-time comparison checks?
options: Use the UTF-8 bytes of the exact environment string
Require a fixed textual encoding such as base64 and compare decoded bytes
Measure Unicode characters and compare text
open_points.default_guess: Use the UTF-8 bytes of the exact, unnormalised environment string.

open_points.subject: Backup encryption and key digest
open_points.text: “Each backup is encrypted with the backup key” and records “a digest of the key,” but no encryption construction, authentication requirement, nonce rule, key interpretation or digest algorithm is declared.
open_points.question: What exact authenticated-encryption and key-digest construction must a release use so that encryption, tamper detection and key identification are testable and interoperable?
options: Declare one authenticated-encryption algorithm, nonce scheme and cryptographic key digest
Allow each implementation or release to choose and record an algorithm identifier
Require confidentiality only, without authenticated encryption
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned authenticated-encryption format with a fresh random nonce and a SHA-256 digest of the exact key bytes.

open_points.subject: Backup metadata for an empty audit log
open_points.text: A backup records “the last audit sequence number it holds” and its check requires “that its audit log ends at the recorded sequence number,” but a new store can have no audit entry and therefore no last sequence number.
open_points.question: What value is recorded and what check is performed when the audit log is empty?
options: Record 0 and require that no audit entry exists
Record an explicit absent/null value
Refuse to keep a backup until at least one audit entry exists
open_points.default_guess: Record 0 and verify that the log contains no entries and the stored sequence counter is zero.

open_points.subject: Backup retention cutoff
open_points.text: The cleanup deletes backups “made more than 30 × 24 hours before,” while a run has no bounded duration; the text does not say whether age is evaluated at the run’s start, at the beginning of cleanup or separately when each file is examined.
open_points.question: Which instant defines the 30-day cutoff for every file in one backup run?
options: Fix one cutoff from the run’s start instant
Fix one cutoff when the cleanup step begins
Evaluate age separately at each file’s deletion check
open_points.default_guess: Fix one cutoff from the run’s start instant and use it for the entire run.

open_points.subject: One backup run per UTC date
open_points.text: A run occurs when the process sees 03:00 and “no kept backup of that date exists,” and “a restart ... or a clock set back makes no second run,” but a failed run leaves no kept backup and no model records that the date was already attempted.
open_points.question: After a failed run, how is a prior attempt remembered across a clock rollback or restart so that the same UTC date cannot run twice?
options: Persist the last attempted UTC date in the store
Remember attempts only in process memory, allowing a retry after restart
Let only a kept backup suppress another run, so failed runs may repeat that date
open_points.default_guess: Persist the last attempted UTC date in the store, separate from the backup files.

open_points.subject: Clock jumps across several backup times
open_points.text: A run is made when the process “sees the clock pass 03:00 of that date,” but the rules do not cover a forward clock jump that crosses 03:00 for more than one UTC date.
open_points.question: Does such a jump cause one run for the current date, one run for every crossed date, or no run because those scheduled instants were missed?
options: Run once for the current UTC date
Run once for every crossed UTC date, sequentially
Treat all crossed scheduled instants as missed and wait for the next 03:00
open_points.default_guess: Run once for the current UTC date and do not backfill earlier crossed dates.
